cases.scenario: A team asks for a lead conversion model. The usable history contains 214 conversions across 14 months, below the 500-positive working floor.
pass_if: States the positive count and the floor it sits below, with the floor named as a working rule of thumb rather than a law
Gives the detectable effect size at this sample rather than only saying 'not enough data'
Produces a usable rule-based alternative computed from the same history, with its n
Names the specific condition that changes the verdict (positives reaching the floor) and roughly when
Recommends starting point-in-time feature snapshot logging now
fail_if: Refuses with no number and no alternative
Builds and reports a model AUC as if it were decisive at this sample size
Presents the 500-positive floor as an absolute prohibition

cases.scenario: A submitted opportunity-win model reports 0.96 test AUC. Its top feature is 'days in current stage', computed against the current date.
pass_if: Identifies the result as implausible against the 0.68-0.80 prior band for this problem and says it is a prior, not a law
Names the specific leakage mechanism: recency computed against now() on a closed record measures time since close
Prescribes the ablation test and the point-in-time replay as the confirmations
States the expected honest performance range after the fix
Does not claim the model is worthless without running the check
fail_if: Accepts 0.96 AUC as a good result
Rejects the model outright with no diagnosis and no test
Attributes the result to overfitting generically without naming the leaking feature

cases.scenario: An analyst proposes an 80/20 random split on an opportunity dataset where accounts appear multiple times.
pass_if: Rejects the random split and names both failure modes: future leakage and entity leakage across the split
Prescribes a grouped temporal split with an embargo of at least one label horizon
States that the embargo exists because recent records' outcomes have not resolved and would enter as false negatives
Gives the positive-rate-by-recent-week query as the check that the embargo is sized correctly
fail_if: Prescribes only a temporal split without entity grouping

cases.scenario: A team wants a model to prioritise a list of 40 enterprise accounts per quarter for a human-reviewed outbound programme.
pass_if: Recommends against a model and names the reasons from the gate: low volume, per-case human review, explanation outweighing marginal lift
Proposes the concrete alternative: a ranked list on the known-good fields with the ranking logic stated
States the condition under which the answer would change
Does not frame the recommendation as a limitation of the tooling
fail_if: Declines to give any prioritisation method

cases.scenario: MQL definition changed nine months into an eighteen-month training window. The user asks for a model over the full window.
pass_if: Identifies that the window spans two label definitions and that training across the seam trains on two different problems
Offers both routes: restrict to the post-change window, or recompute the earlier period under the new definition from raw fields
States the cost of each route in positives available
Requires the label version to be recorded and any crossing trendline to be marked
fail_if: Trains across the seam without comment
Treats the definition change as a data-quality problem to be cleaned rather than a modelling decision

cases.scenario: A stakeholder reports that their churn model is '97% accurate' on a 3% churn base rate.
pass_if: States that predicting no-churn for every record also scores 97% on this base rate, giving the number
Rejects accuracy for this problem explicitly
Names the metrics that answer the question: precision-recall, top-decile lift, calibration
Asks for the baseline comparison rather than dismissing the model
fail_if: Dismisses the model without showing why the metric is uninformative
